Native modal interference was independently demonstrated by the main reviewer, with attribution preserved below. No frozen implementation or test file was changed.
method.historyBoundary: web/VERIFICATION.md is an assigned current document and contains historical repair/test summaries. Read that document itself only; did not open its linked historical reports. The current-round root-browser.json contains screenshot aliases for other checks; only its attachment-modal reproduction is used here, and none of those other image paths was opened.

findings.title: Release nested attachment preview modal ownership when authentication expires
findings.explanation: App retains Workspace under a hidden wrapper when authentication becomes false so that drafts survive renewal. Workspace clears its own modal/mobile/branchAction states, but the AttachmentButton inside the retained Composer owns a separate preview state and has no authentication/active input. Its Dialog remains mounted and open. Native showModal ownership survives the hidden ancestor and makes the visible login page inert. The ordinary password-field login interaction is therefore blocked exactly when the session must be renewed.
reproduction: Open the current application with a valid session and a draft attachment; use the attachment button to open its preview dialog.
While the preview is open, let the session check become authenticated=false after the WebSocket connection closes.
The login page becomes visible, while the attachment dialog remains connected, open, modal, and inside the hidden Workspace wrapper.
In the main reviewer native-browser fixture, click the visible administrator password field: focus remains BODY and the accessibility tree contains only the root.
findings.expected: Authentication loss releases all modal/top-layer ownership, including nested attachment previews, while retaining the unsent draft.
findings.impact: Session renewal controls cannot be focused through the ordinary visible login flow. This is a reproducible UI availability failure; no claim of data loss or permanent account lockout is made.

evidence.result: Current App under jsdom: dialogStillConnected=true, dialogOpen=true, hasHiddenAncestor=true, loginPresent=true, draftRetained="Unsent draft", mutationCalls=[]. showModal/close are polyfilled, so this alone establishes lifecycle state rather than native inertness.

evidence.source: main reviewer independent validation supplied during this round
evidence.result: Current production UI with only a 59-byte local synthetic text attachment: modalSelectorMatched=true, hiddenAncestor=true, passwordInputCount=1, activeElementAfterPasswordClick=BODY, accessibilityTreeOnlyRoot=true. Isolated loopback fixture and browser tab were stopped after reproduction.

findings.recommendation: Make nested preview modal ownership follow the active/authenticated workspace lifetime, closing or unmounting the preview when access expires without discarding the draft. Add an auth-loss lifecycle regression through the attachment preview entry point; the existing settings-modal lifecycle test does not cover this nested owner.

consideredCandidates.topic: Image dimension admission differs between attachment preview and message media
consideredCandidates.disposition: Not promoted to a finding: insufficient demonstrated product-contract violation or concrete adverse impact.
consideredCandidates.evidence: AttachmentButton admits only four raster MIME types for inline preview and limits returned base64 length to 6,000,000, but does not parse dimensions. web/lib/media.ts has a 16,384-per-dimension and 40,000,000-pixel admission limit. Runtime reviewer independently reported canonical base64, 4 MiB per attachment, total 128 MiB/128 item bounds and no upstream pixel parser; that runtime body was not independently inspected by this reviewer.
consideredCandidates.reasoning: The assigned current web/VERIFICATION.md states attachment limits of 8 per draft, 4 MiB per file and 64 KiB text preview, without declaring a uniform image-pixel budget for this attachment path. The reviewed difference alone does not prove that a normal permitted local-file workflow violates a promised resource bound. No OOM, decoder denial of service, or cross-authority content impact was demonstrated. No memory-intensive browser decompression experiment was performed.

validations.scope: Existing affected regression tests; the nested attachment/auth-loss gap is independently reproduced, so this pass is not claimed to refute the finding.

limitations: This report covers the assigned 198-file gateway-core/web-ux partition in full; it is not an independent review of the other 1,587 frozen source files.

No full test suite, Linux/systemd/SSH integration, live service/provider execution, paid inference, real external MCP, personal configuration or credential access was performed. These are post-audit integration boundaries, not skipped tests represented as passing.
All assigned test bodies were reviewed, but only the listed three exact test files were executed. Static review of other tests does not imply their runtime success.
The reviewer-owned jsdom fixture does not implement the browser top layer or native inertness. Those assertions rely on the separately attributed main-reviewer browser evidence.
Image decompression/resource impact remains unverified as explained in consideredCandidates; absence of a promoted finding is not a claim that arbitrary image dimensions are safe.
No fix was made to the frozen implementation or tests. The confirmed modal-lifetime issue remains actionable.
